    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.not_isBGRSSpecialZero_of_right_isIso {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≠ 0) (e : Y ⟶ Z) [CategoryTheory.IsIso e] :
    ¬IsBGRSSpecialZero f e

    A nonzero morphism followed by an isomorphism cannot be a BGRS special pair. Cancellation reduces a hypothetical special equation to multiplication by 1-rho, which is invertible for rho in the Jacobson radical.

      theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.raySourceIncomparable_representatives_of_irreducible {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [HasWellDefinedBGRSRayProduct C] {X Y Z : C} (a : X ⟶ Y) (ha0 : a ≠ 0) (f : X ⟶ Z) (hf0 : f ≠ 0) (ha : IsIrreducibleRayMorphism a) (hf : IsIrreducibleRayMorphism f) (hinc : RaySourceIncomparable (unitRayNonzeroHom a ha0) (unitRayNonzeroHom f hf0)) :
      RaySourceIncomparable ⟨a, ha0⟩ ⟨f, hf0⟩

      Source incomparability of two irreducible rays lifts to source incomparability of any nonzero ordinary representatives. In a hypothetical factorization, irreducibility makes the remaining factor invertible, so the BGRS product agrees with ordinary composition.
